JUDGMENT

By this judgment this Tribunal shall decide the petition filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1989 seeking compensation of Rs.40,00,000/- in respect of injuries sustained by her in the Road Traffic Accident.

2. It is the case of the petitioner that, on 23.03.2023 at about 6.25 p.m, petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider in a vehicle Pleasure Scooty bearing reg. no.AP-03-BN-5782 near Penumur Cross,
Chittoor Mandal along with one K.Pushpalatha who was riding the Scooty , at that time one Yamaha R15 motor cycle bearing reg.No.AP-39-HH-1700 which was proceeding towards Chittoor coming from Puthalapattu side and lost control over Yamaha motor cycle and dashed to the Scooty which was coming from Chittoor Vishnu hospital.
Due to the impact, petitioner fell down on the road and sustained bleeding (SCCH-12) 3 MVC. No.3943/2024 injuries to her right leg and other injuries all over the body.
The motor cycle was also damaged.
3. Immediately petitioner was shifted to Govt.Hospital, Chittoor for treatment, after first aid she was shifted to Sri Sai Sudha hospitals, Tirupati for further treatment.
She was treated as inpatient from 24.03.2023 to 29.03.2023.

That she sustained, sutured wound over left knee measuring 4 X 1 cm,
(2) sutured wound + over head (3) multiple superficial abrasion + over right shoulder, left ankle,
right knee, face and swelling + tenderness over left knee and other injuries all over the body.
Petitioner has undergone operation with an advice for follow up treatment.

Petitioner was once again readmitted to the said hospital as inpatient form 12.05.2023 to 19.05.2023.
4.
It is further stated in the petition that petitioner was hale and healthy and she was an Agriculturist cum coolie and she was earning Rs.30,000/- per annum.
The accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the drive of Motor cycle bearing reg.No.AP-39-HH-1700.
The Chittoor Taluk police have filed charge sheet against the driver for negligence act U/s.337 of IPC in Crime no.48/2023.
The 1st respondent is the R.C owner and 2nd respondent is the insurer are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
On all these grounds, she prayed to allow the petition and award compensation.
On issuance of notice, respondent no.1 is served.
He remained absent to the court.
Hence, he is placed ex-parte.
6. 2nd respondent appeared through counsel and filed written statement contending that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
That insured has not complied Sec.134(c) of M.V.Act, concerned police have not complied Sec.159 of the said Act.
It seeks protection under Section 147 and 149 of M.V.Act.
That the rider of motor cycle was not holding valid and effective driving license to ride the motor cycle as on the date of accident.

The 1 st respondent being owner of motor cycle has committed breach of terms and conditions of policy willfully and entrusted the motor cycle to a person who was riding without holding valid and effective driving license.

That it Rajeswari.K vs Govardhan.G on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172453701/
2 has not issued policy of insurance in favour of 1st respondent in respect of motor cycle bearing no.AP-39-HH-1700 and the liability of it is limited to the terms and conditions of policy, D.L, R.C and F.C of the petitioner.
Age, occupation, physical disability and medical expenses alleged are denied.
On all these grounds he prayed to dismiss the petition.
7. On the basis of above pleadings, following issues are framed:-
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that on 23.03.2023 at about 6.25 pm petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider in Pleasure Scooty bearing Reg.No.AP-03-BN-5782 near Penumur (SCCH-12) 5 MVC. No.3943/2024 cross, Chittoor Mandal along with one K.Pushpalatha who was riding the said vehicle slowly and cautiously by observing traffic rules at that time, one Motor cycle bearing reg. no.AP- 39-HH-1700 ridden by its rider in high speed and rash and negligent manner and hit the scooty in which petitioner was pillion rider, due to which petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries as alleged?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?

If so by whom and what is the quantum?
3. What Order or Award?
8. To prove her case, petitioner entered witness box and got examined as P.W.1.
Through her Ex.P.1 to P.13 documents are marked.
On the other hand, representative of 2 nd respondent insurance company got examined as R.W.1.
Through him Ex.R1 and 2 documents are marked and closed his side evidence.
9. Both side remained absent for arguments.
Hence, arguments taken as nil and case is taken up for judgment.
Perused the records.

Issue No.1: Partly in the Affirmative, Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3:

sentences.text: To prove this fact, petitioner entered witness box and got examined as P.W.1.
In her affidavit she reiterated petition averments.

She has produced FIR, first information, translated copy of first information, police intimation, accident investigation report, rough sketch, wound certificate and final report along with discharge summary.
12. On perusal of those documents it can be seen that son of petitioner is first informant and he is not eye witness to the case.

He stated that his wife and mother had went to hospital on 23.03.2023 along with his son for treatment and while coming back at 6.30 pm the motor cycle rider who is wife of this first informant sustained accident by rash and negligent driving of the rider of one motor cycle bearing AP-39-HH-1700.
This petitioner was pillion rider on the motor cycle of the wife of first informant and she sustained grievous injuries.

It is stated that the rider of AP-39-HH-1700 was rash and negligent in riding and action may be taken against him.
13.
On the basis of that first information Chittor police have registered Crime No.48/2023 against aforesaid bike rider for the offence of negligence.
They have prepared accident information report along with rough sketch.
As per the rough (SCCH-12) 7 MVC. No.3943/2024 sketch accident was taken place in the middle of the road where there is cross on the right side from Chittoor towards Tirupati.
It is stated in the petition that, the opponent bike rider was coming from Puthalapattu side and going towards Chittoor and the petitioner was coming from Chittoor and going towards Penamuru.
That shows the accident has taken place in the middle of the road near the cross as per the spot sketch.
If the petitioner bike rider was some more cautious while taking right turn towards Penamur cross, the accident could have been avoided.
Similarly the bike rider was also were to be more cautious, the accident could have been avoided.
Since it is head on collusion in the middle of the road, there is negligence on part of the petitioner bike rider.
As per the charge sheet, the opponent rider had no D.L and he was also negligent in riding the bike.
The opponent bike rider-cum-owner has not appeared to contest the case or to produce his D.L before the court.

P.W.1 who is eye witness to the incident and also victim of the accident has denied negligence on part of her daughter-in-law who is bike rider and attributed negligence to opponent Yamaha bike rider, but spot sketch produced by her shows negligence on part of the daughter-in-law of petitioner.

Therefore, in the opinion of this court the negligence on part of petitioner bike rider is 10% and opponent rider of the bike bearing no.AP-39- HH-1700 is 90%. Accordingly, this issue is answered Partly in the Affirmative.
(SCCH-12) 8 MVC. No.3943/2024 14. ISSUE NO.2 : To prove his age petitioner has produced aadhaar card at Ex.P.8 which shows her year of birth as 1966.
Accident took place on 23.03.2023.
She was aged 58 years at the time of accident.
Therefore, the age of the petitioner is considered as 58 years at the time of accident.

4 15.
In respect of occupation it is stated that, petitioner was an Agriculturist-cum coolie and was earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
To prove this fact she has not produced document.
Hence notional income has to be considered.
The accident took place in the year 2023.
Therefore monthly income of the petitioner is held as Rs.16,000/-.
In respect of permanent disability petitioner has not led any evidence.
Therefore, it is held that there is no functional disability affecting the income of petitioner.

Hence, the quantum of compensation is determined as under:
(i) Medical expenses:
The petitioner has produced medical bill of Sri Sai Sudhal hospital at Ex.

As per the evidence of P.W.1 amount paid by her is Rs.20,586/-
The said payment of bill is due to the accident caused to her.
Therefore, petitioner is entitled for Rs.20,586/-.
(ii) Food and nourishment:
The petitioner has produced Ex.P.11 and 12 discharge summary which shows that she was admitted in Sri Sai Sudha hospital from 24.03.2023 to 29.03.2023.
Surgery was conducted.
She was admitted to the same hospital for a second time i.e., from 12.05.2023 to 19.05.2023 inpatient period for 14 days.

Considering the cost of (SCCH-12) 9 MVC. No.3943/2024 living, food,
nourishment charges if per day Rs.500/- is awarded, Rs.500/- x 14 days =
Rs.7000/-it will meet the ends of justice.
(iii) Attendant charges:
The petitioner sustained compound comminuted supra condylar fracture of femur fracture of left leg and took treatment in hospital.
Someone must have taken care of the petitioner during his treatment period.
Hence, attendant charges of Rs.7,000/- is awarded.
(iv) Loss of income during laid up period:
For the grievous injury of fracture, considering advanced age of the petitioner, laid up period is considered as 4 months.
Hence loss of income during laid up period is Rs.16,000 X 4 months = Rs.64,000/- and the same is awarded under this head.
(v) Conveyance charges:
Petitioner has spent money for conveyance for the purpose of treatment.
Considering the same, this court is of the opinion that amount of Rs.5,000/- shall be awarded as conveyance charges.
(vi) Loss of future income due to Disability : Petitioner has not examined doctor.
There is no evidence regarding physical disability.
As per the findings given above, there is no functional disability affecting the income of the petitioner.
Hence, no compensation is awarded under this head.
(vii) For Future medical expenses: There is no evidence to show that there is need of future medical treatment in respect of the injuries sustained by the petitioner.
Therefore, no compensation is awarded under this head.
(SCCH-12) 10 MVC. No.3943/2024 Rajeswari.K vs Govardhan.G on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172453701/
5 (viii) For Pain and sufferings:
The petitioner has sustained compound comminuted supra condylar fracture of femur fracture of left leg.
She underwent surgery at hospital and suffered pain and agony.
Therefore, for pain and suffering the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.40,000/- .

(ix) Physical discomfort and loss of amenities of life :
Since petitioner suffered fracture to left leg that will affect the normal enjoyment of life.
Therefore, Rs.30,000/- is awarded under this head.
(x) Loss of future prospect:
As per the judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme court, even in injury cases, loss of future prospect has to be considered.

But in the present case,
the on going through the evidence and the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner there is no chance of loss of future prospect.
Hence no compensation is awarded under this head.

Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.1,56,228/- in respect of injuries sustained by him in the Road traffic accident precisely under the following heads;

sentences.text:
The facts of that case were as under:
4.

It is stated that, the claimants have filed a claim petition seeking compensation of Rs.85 lakhs under all the relevant heads with interest at the rate of 12% per annum on account of the death of (SCCH-12) 12 MVC. No.3943/2024 Moulappa in a road traffic accident that occurred on 21.08.2022, when the deceased was proceeding on his motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-53/L-4726 from Masadoddi to Yeragera on Raichur - Mantralaya road and when he was in front of Raichur University bus stop, it is alleged that,
respondent No.1 being the driver of the lorry bearing registration No.MH-10/AQ- 4016 came from opposite direction in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motorcycle of said Moulappa.
Because of this accident, he sustained grievous injuries and died on the spot.

On discussing several other judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme court, the Hon'ble High court has held u as under:
16.
......So far as fastening of liability is concerned, the learned counsel for the appellant - Insurance Company has relied upon the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Pappu (supra).
Evidently, the rider of the motorcycle, who is the deceased was third party to the said accident.
There was no negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle in causing the said accident.

Though the claimants have made the owner as well as driver of the said offending lorry as parties to the claim petition and they have appeared, but have not filed any objections to the claim petition.

When the Insurance Company has taken up a contention that, the driver or owner of the offending lorry ought to have appeared before the Tribunal and produced the driving licence so as to absolve from the liability.
Even the Insurance Company has not summoned the (SCCH-12) 13 MVC.
No.3943/2024 driver and it is the duty of the owner of the lorry to permit the driver, who is possessing effective driving licence.
In this case, either the owner of the lorry or the driver have not entered the witness box.
In the absence of the same, the version of the Insurance Company that, the driver of the said offending lorry was not possessing effective driving licence has to be accepted.

In view of the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Pappu (supra), as per the conditions of the policy, the insured vehicle must be driven by the driver of the vehicle, who is having effective driving licence.
In this case, it is not so.
Therefore, there is a violation of the policy conditions by the owner of the lorry.
As M.V. Act is a benevolent legislation, the claimants cannot be deprived of the Rajeswari.K vs Govardhan.

G on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172453701/
7 compensation so awarded in this case.

Therefore, if the Insurance Company is directed to deposit the compensation, as the policy was in force as on the date of accident, as the Insurance Company has to indemnify the said compensation so awarded in view the principle laid down in the aforesaid judgments by the Hon'ble Apex Court, it would meet the ends of justice.
However, the Insurance Company is at liberty to recover the same from the owner of the lorry by executing the award against him.
Hence, the appeal to that extent, is to be allowed in part.
In this decision the date of accident was 21.08.2022 which is subsequent to the said amendment.
On that date the policy was in force as per the facts of that case.

Therefore pay and (SCCH-12) 14 MVC.
No.3943/2024 recovery was ordered.
In the present case also policy is existing as on the date of accident and rider of the offending vehicle had no D.L.
Therefore, applying this decision it is proper to order pay and recovery.
Accordingly, this issue is answered Partly in the Affirmative.
17. ISSUE NO.3 :

In view of above reasons I proceed to pass following;
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner u/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.
It is held that, petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.1,56,228/- with interest @ 6% pa from the date of petition till the date of payment.

Respondent no.2 insurance company is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner and hereby directed to deposit the aforesaid compensation amount with interest before this tribunal within one month from the date of this order and then entitled to recover the said amount from the owner of the offending vehicle i.e. 1st respondent on the principle of pay and recovery.
(SCCH-12) 15 MVC. No.3943/2024  On such deposit, the petitioner is entitled to have release of entire amount on her proper identification.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Award be drawn accordingly.
